meta.desc: Mindfulness according to science: why your mind wanders almost half the day, what mindfulness is and where it comes from, the one-minute cyclic sigh, why slowing down helps you get more done, what studies say and what they don’t, how to meditate even if you can’t stop thinking, and a plan to make the calm stay.

lista.noHuirDet: It’s looking at it head-on, with curiosity and without judging yourself.
lista.moderadoDet: It helps with anxiety, depression and pain, but it isn’t magic.
lista.noMejorDet: In the 2014 review it performed about like exercise or therapy, not better.

lista.resumen1: Your mind wanders almost half the day
lista.resumen2: Mindfulness is noticing and coming back, without judging
lista.resumen3: Breathing slowly calms your body, and slowing down helps you get more done
lista.resumen4: A few minutes every day are worth more than an hour now and then

grafica.mes1Det: Blocks for the important, with breaks and a buffer
grafica.revisionDet: Fifteen minutes: empty, rearrange and plan

cierre.titulo: Your time, in your own house
cierre.texto: In the Schedule room in MindHaOS you jot down your to-dos, move them on a board, give them a date and time so they show up in your calendar with a reminder, and keep track of your people’s birthdays and care, along with the missions from your other rooms.

paquete.guia: Interactive guide (with the planning fallacy, the to-do tray, the Eisenhower matrix, the cost of switching tasks, a kanban board, your week in blocks, the Pomodoro technique and a buffer for the unexpected, all moving in your browser)
paquete.app: Open the Schedule room in MindHaOS
